endorsements.quote: Strong data governance was also highlighted, especially the importance of maintaining separation between training and testing datasets to prevent data leakage and reduce the potential risk of model overfitting.

Other suggested approaches included using synthetic data to fill gaps — while acknowledging its limitations — and validating data through independent external partners not involved in initial development.
Developers should incorporate bias mitigation strategies during initial model development and conduct ongoing monitoring to detect any unexpected biases.

unlisted_practices: Collect extensive, representative data across all relevant areas when developing AI models.
Test AI models across various demographics to identify weaknesses.
Implement human oversight and review of AI, particularly for high-risk applications.
Document limitations in the data used to develop AI models.
Adopt standardized data models and vocabularies and develop frameworks to assess real-world data quality for AI model development.
Establish collaborative, secure data-sharing platforms such as federated computing that protect patient privacy and intellectual property.
Use explainable AI techniques, human-in-the-loop methods, independent verification of results, and sensitivity analyses to address limited interpretability.
Ensure end users can understand and effectively use AI outputs.
Clearly communicate the methods used in AI models to stakeholders to build trust.
Regulators should adopt a flexible, risk-based approach to AI oversight proportionate to risk and tailored to context of use.
Regulators should publish high-level principles and guidance supported by FAQs, white papers, and illustrative examples.
Start with small, low-risk AI use cases and share case studies to demonstrate risk-based approaches.
Pursue international harmonization of AI regulations and terminology.
Involve multidisciplinary experts in developing AI tools.
Establish standardized AI terminology across disciplines through joint efforts.
Increase AI literacy across the drug development community and tailor communication to specific audiences.
Develop multidisciplinary expertise through cross-disciplinary training and incentives.
Encourage public-private partnerships for responsible data sharing.
Develop standards for data quality and fitness for use, including guidance on synthetic data.

screen.reason: Workshop report synthesizing regulatory perspectives and guiding principles from the FDA and CTTI on AI in drug and biological product development.
